---
title: "README"
subtitle: "Sex differences in how elevated temperatures affect immune response"

## Overview

This repository contains the data and analysis code for the manuscript "Sex differences in
how elevated temperatures affect immune response" (Fu, Head, Iglesias-Carrasco, MacNamara &
Chung). The study uses a multigenerational experiment with the seed beetle (*Callosobruchus
maculatus*) in which maternal, paternal and offspring developmental temperatures were
independently manipulated (control = 25°C, coded "C"; elevated = 31°C, coded "H"), and tests
how these temperatures affect two components of offspring innate immunity: phenoloxidase (PO)
activity and lytic (antibacterial) activity.

All statistics and figures reported in the manuscript are produced by
`Beetle_analysis_script.Rmd`. That script is kept intentionally minimal (code and short
in-line comments only); this README holds the fuller explanations, the data dictionary, and a
map from each script section to the corresponding table/figure in the manuscript.

## Repository contents

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `Beetle_analysis_script.Rmd` | Analysis code: data cleaning, standardisation, mixed models, figures, and effect sizes. |
| `raw_data.csv` | Raw dataset (n = 1740 individuals sampled; see manuscript Table S1 for sample sizes per treatment combination). |
| `README.Rmd` / `README.md` | This file. |

## Data dictionary (`raw_data.csv`)

One row = one offspring beetle sampled for immune assays. Columns used in the analysis
script:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Mum_temp`, `Dad_temp` | Rearing temperature of the mother/father ("C" = control/ancestral 25°C, "H" = high/elevated 31°C) |
| `OS_temp` | Offspring (developmental) rearing temperature (same "C"/"H" coding) |
| `Sex` | Offspring sex ("F"/"M") |
| `OS_age` | Offspring age at sampling, in days post-eclosion (1, 3, 5 or 7) |
| `Weight` | Offspring body weight (mg) at collection |
| `PO_Activity`, `PO_interplate`, `PO_Plate_ID` | Raw PO activity (OD/min), the matched inter-plate control value, and plate ID (used to standardise PO activity within plate) |
| `Zone_Area_1/2/3`, `Zone_Clarity`, `Lytic_Interplate`, `Lytic_Plate_ID` | Triplicate raw inhibition-zone measurements, a qualitative clarity score, the inter-plate control, and plate ID for the lytic assay |
| `Mother` | Maternal family ID, fitted as the random effect (siblings share a mother) |

## Analysis approach

For both PO activity and lytic activity, and for each sex separately (to avoid overfitting;
see Methods), the script fits linear mixed models (`lme4::lmer`) with maternal, paternal and
developmental temperature and their interactions as fixed effects, offspring age (ordered
factor) and body weight as covariates, and mother (family) ID as a random intercept. Lytic
models additionally include inhibition-zone clarity as a covariate. Each model starts as the
full three-way-interaction model and is simplified by removing non-significant higher-order
interactions in turn (Type III Wald chi-square tests via `car::Anova`); the final reduced
model is compared against the full model with a likelihood-ratio test
(`anova(..., REML = FALSE)`). Where a significant maternal-by-paternal interaction remains,
pairwise comparisons use Tukey-adjusted contrasts (`emmeans`).

PO activity is standardised (within-plate correction against the inter-plate control) and
log-transformed before modelling. Lytic activity is standardised the same way but left on the
raw scale, since raw-scale residuals met the normality/homoscedasticity assumptions (assessed
via Q-Q plots; see Methods).

Effect sizes (Cohen's d, control vs. high developmental temperature) are calculated separately
for females and males for both responses, and the two sexes' effect sizes are compared with a
Welch-style t-test, matching the "Sex difference" paragraphs in the manuscript Results.

## How to run

1. Open the folder containing `Beetle_analysis_script.Rmd` and `raw_data.csv` as the
   working directory (e.g. via an RStudio Project) before knitting/running the script — it
   reads `raw_data.csv` using a relative path.
2. Run the script top to bottom. The first chunk installs any missing packages.
3. Analyses reported in the manuscript were run in R 4.5.1 (R Core Team) within RStudio
   2025.05.1. Package versions used are not pinned in the script; when archiving results,
   record `sessionInfo()` output alongside the script.
